record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.context_brief: Two nested caustics and the ellipse problem
record.original_question: Suppose a bounded strictly convex planar billiard has two nested closed caustics with the property that the smaller caustic is itself a caustic for the billiard in the larger caustic. Does this already force the billiard boundary to be an ellipse?

evidence.quote: Question (Konstantin Khanin, August 2019): Suppose that a bounded strictly convex planar billiard has just two nested closed caustics satisfying the above condition: the smaller caustic is a caustic for the billiard in the bigger one. Is it true that the billiard boundary is an ellipse?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded strictly convex domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and consider the billiard inside $\Omega$ (a point particle moves along straight lines and reflects off $\partial\Omega$ according to the law that angle of incidence equals angle of reflection). A closed smooth convex curve $\gamma \subset \Omega$ is called a caustic of the billiard in $\Omega$ if every billiard trajectory tangent to $\gamma$ remains tangent to $\gamma$ after each reflection off $\partial\Omega$.

Suppose that the billiard in $\Omega$ admits two nested closed caustics $\gamma_1 \subset \gamma_2 \subset \Omega$ (with $\gamma_1$ strictly inside the region bounded by $\gamma_2$) with the following compatibility property: $\gamma_1$ is itself a caustic for the billiard in the convex domain bounded by $\gamma_2$ (i.e., trajectories inside $\gamma_2$ tangent to $\gamma_1$ remain tangent to $\gamma_1$ after reflection off $\gamma_2$).

Must $\partial\Omega$ be an ellipse?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to be a known open question related to the Birkhoff conjecture and Poritsky's property. Poritsky/Amiran proved rigidity under the stronger hypothesis that every pair of nested caustics has this property; the two-caustic version remains an open question, with related recent work on algebraic caustics by Glutsyuk and others not resolving it.

status_evidence.title: Four equivalent properties of integrable billiards (Glutsyuk)
status_evidence.snippet: Poritsky's property: for every two nested caustics the smaller one is a caustic for the billiard in the bigger one; this implies the boundary is an ellipse.
status_evidence.claim: Rigidity is known when the property holds for ALL pairs of nested caustics, but the two-caustic version stated here is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: On complex algebraic caustics in planar and projective billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work discusses open problems regarding pairs of nested ovals with the caustic compatibility property distinct from confocal ellipses.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether two nested compatible caustics force the boundary to be an ellipse remains discussed as open.
